blocks.text: Cates Landing — Cates Landing Way, addresses including 3825, 3873 and 3911 Cates Landing Way, off Dollarton Highway beside Whey-ah-Wichen (Cates Park) (District of North Vancouver; MLS sub-area: Roche Point)

A 4-storey waterfront complex by Polygon (Polygon Cates Landing Ltd.), designed by Keith Hemphill of Rositch Hemphill Architects, built/completed in 2017 (some later-phase units are listed as built 2018 — the phase split is UNCONFIRMED). Current listings describe freehold strata title, wood-frame construction, and amenities including a fitness room, guest suite, bike room, kayak storage, dog wash, meeting rooms and an on-site building manager. Published restrictions: the building directory states pets allowed with restrictions; a current listing describes the complex as "pet & rental friendly." Age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Streets, schools and getting around Dollarton

items.t: Dollarton is the District of North Vancouver area along Dollarton Highway on the north shore of Burrard Inlet, between Maplewood at the west end and Deep Cove to the east. The port authority's shoreline report places Maplewood Flats at the west end, the Tsleil-Waututh Nation reserve lands (Burrard Inlet IR #3) along the shore backed by Dollarton Highway, and Whey-ah-Wichen (Cates Park) farther east. A single District boundary line for the whole sub-area beyond that shoreline description is UNVERIFIED.

Where the condo stock actually concentrates: in one place only — Cates Landing, the Polygon complex on Cates Landing Way beside Whey-ah-Wichen (Cates Park) at the east end of the shore. The rest of Dollarton is detached houses on R1 and R2 lots along and above Dollarton Highway; a neighbourhood source describes Dollarton as almost entirely detached, with condo and townhome inventory minimal and rare when it appears. The attached stock at the west end (Maplewood Village Centre, Old Dollarton Road) is Maplewood, not Dollarton, and is excluded in.

Transit anchors: TransLink route 211 (Phibbs Exchange / Burrard Station) runs via Dollarton Highway between Deep Cove and Phibbs Exchange, with some trips continuing to Burrard Station; route 212 runs via Dollarton Highway and Main Street to Phibbs Exchange; route 215 (Indian River) runs via Main Street, Dollarton Highway and Old Dollarton Road, then Riverside Drive and Mount Seymour Parkway. The R2 RapidBus connects at Phibbs Exchange and, since September 7, 2026, runs one-seat from Park Royal through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station.

Anchors inside and beside the area: Whey-ah-Wichen (Cates Park), 4141 Dollarton Highway, is the waterfront park beside the condo complex; Parkgate Community Centre (3625 Banff Court) and the Parkgate library branch (3675 Banff Court) are north of the area; no public school inside Dollarton itself is confirmed — Cove Cliff Elementary (1818 Banbury Road) and Seycove Secondary (1204 Caledonia Avenue) are in Deep Cove to the east, and Seymour Heights Elementary (2640 Carnation Street) is to the north-west.

items.t: Shoreline and foreshore — the Dollarton-specific layer: the port authority states the Whey-ah-Wichen (Cates Park) shoreline is eroding and likely to worsen with sea level rise and climate change, and a shoreline adaptation and restoration project at the park, proposed by the District and the Tsleil-Waututh Nation, is under review by the port authority. Burrard Inlet waters and the intertidal area are federal lands and waters managed by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority — dock, seawall or foreshore work is not a District-only approval. District OCP Schedule B also sets Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside, Wildfire, Creek and Slope Hazard Development Permit Areas, and the District publishes GeoWeb flood construction levels modelled to a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m.
The sub-area's only condo complex is filed under a different sub-area.

Whey-ah-Wichen (Cates Park) holds important cultural significance for the Tsleil-Waututh Nation, Burrard Inlet's waters are port-authority jurisdiction, and the proposed shoreline adaptation and restoration project there is a District / Tsleil-Waututh proposal under port-authority review — waterfront work near the complex sits inside that process, not just District permitting.
The west end is planned to change, and it is Maplewood's plan, not Dollarton's.

The fastest bus on the North Shore now connects at Dollarton's exchange. Since September 7, 2026 the R2 RapidBus runs one-seat from Park Royal through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station — Dollarton's routes 211/212/215 all feed Phibbs.

There is no school inside the sub-area. Despite the family-house stock, no public school in Dollarton itself is confirmed on SD44's pages — the named schools are all in Deep Cove or up in the Seymour pocket, and catchment must be run address by address.

One developer-era number, two forms. Listings and directories often quote Cates Landing as "95 homes" without the split — 80 of those are apartments and 15 are townhouses, and the two forms price, insure and resell differently inside the same strata.

items.t: Form B diligence (the Cates Landing strata — apartments and its townhouse component alike): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. At Cates Landing, read the Form B together with the building's shoreline and insurance position below — the park shoreline beside it is documented as eroding.
Fee-simple homes (the shore's house stock): No fee-simple townhouse complex is verified here, so this rule is stated for the house form, not misapplied to a counted complex.
The sub-area's only strata complex is filed under a different sub-area (checked Nov 1, 2026).

Whey-ah-Wichen (Cates Park), 4141 Dollarton Highway, holds important cultural significance for the Tsleil-Waututh Nation, Burrard Inlet's waters are port-authority jurisdiction, and the proposed shoreline adaptation and restoration project there is a District / Tsleil-Waututh proposal under port-authority review — waterfront work near the complex sits inside that process, not just District permitting.

There is no school inside the sub-area (researched Nov 1, 2026). Despite the family-house stock, no public school in Dollarton itself is confirmed on SD44's pages — the named schools are all in Deep Cove or up in the Seymour pocket, and catchment must be run address by address.

One headline number, two forms (checked Nov 1, 2026). Listings and directories often quote Cates Landing as "95 homes" without the split — 80 of those are apartments and 15 are townhouses, and the two forms price, insure and resell differently inside the same strata.

The waterfront setback is a number, not a guideline (researched Nov 1, 2026). Under Zoning Bylaw 3210, Section 525, waterfront principal buildings must sit at least 7.6 m back from the Ocean Natural Boundary Line — the lot-level fact behind every Dollarton waterfront listing, and the first measurement to verify on a townhouse yard or house lot opening onto the inlet.

Established shore lots: detached houses on R1 and R2 lots along and above Dollarton Highway; the port authority's shoreline report notes the shore is backed by residential properties. Predominantly freehold detached in the sources read.

Lot character from the zone ladder, as stated: District Zoning Bylaw 3210, Section 525 (Bylaw 8799) — R1 minimum lot 4,000 m² with 30 m width and 34 m depth; R2 minimum lot 660 m² with 18 m width and 34 m depth; modifiers R2(S1) at 335 m² / 10 m, R2(S2) at 1,100 m² / 24 m and R2(S3) at 4,000 m² / 30 m. The R1/R2 setback table sets a minimum setback to the Ocean Natural Boundary Line of 7.6 m for a principal building — directly relevant on Dollarton's waterfront lots. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size; the zone on a single lot is confirmed through the District's GeoWeb.

Serviced position, as the District states it: District single-family utility fees in 2026 include water at $932.80 and sewer/drainage at $1,255.60, with combined single-family utilities of $2,571.20 in 2026. Parcel-level septic or well status: UNVERIFIED.
ALR vs non-ALR: parcel-level ALR status: UNVERIFIED in the research. No ALR percentage split is stated; check any parcel on ALC mapping.

Shoreline / hazard position: the port authority states the Whey-ah-Wichen (Cates Park) shoreline is eroding and likely to worsen with sea level rise and climate change, threatening archaeological resources, shoreline habitat, park infrastructure and cultural sites; a shoreline adaptation and restoration project at the park is proposed by the District of North Vancouver and the Tsleil-Waututh Nation and is under review by the port authority. District OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B sets Development Permit Areas including Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard, and the District publishes property-level GeoWeb reports including modelled flood construction levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m. The waters of Burrard Inlet, including the intertidal area along this shore, fall within federal lands and waters managed by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority — foreshore work is not a District-only approval.
No bare-land strata plan in Dollarton was verified

Cates Landing — cross-reference only, counted in CONDOS only: the apartment homes by Polygon Cates Landing Ltd. Named townhome complexes beyond that record: UNVERIFIED (none confirmed by name in the research).

Maplewood Village Centre (west end) — plan position, documented AS SUCH: the District OCP plans Old Dollarton Road, at the west end of Dollarton, with retail businesses and apartments and live/work units above as a pedestrian-activity focus — a plan designation for the west end, documented as such, never as for-sale lot inventory.

Whey-ah-Wichen shoreline adaptation project — documented AS SUCH: the District / Tsleil-Waututh Nation shoreline adaptation and restoration project at Cates Park, under review by the port authority — a shoreline project on park and reserve shore, not a land offering.

Historic subdivision fabric = built lot fabric, not offerings: the Dollarton Highway lots are established fee-simple lot fabric documented above; no historic subdivision is presented as a lot offering.

items.t: Nearby areas: Maplewood and Maplewood Village Centre (west), Deep Cove (east, along Dollarton Highway), Seymour / Indian River and the Dorothy Lynas streets (north, up Riverside Drive and Mount Seymour Parkway), and — across Burrard Inlet — Belcarra and Port Moody's north shore (south).

Parks, recreation and services: Whey-ah-Wichen (Cates Park), 4141 Dollarton Highway, is a large waterfront park that holds important cultural significance for the Tsleil-Waututh people; the District lists Cates Park / Whey-ah-Wichen among its parks with high regional use. Maplewood Flats, at the west end, is described in the port authority's shoreline report as a large sediment shelf and the remnants of a large wetland complex; the conservation area's operator and visitor facilities are UNVERIFIED. Parkgate Community Centre, 3625 Banff Court, north of the area, is the nearest full-service recreation centre, beside the Parkgate branch library, 3675 Banff Court; a library branch inside Dollarton is UNVERIFIED (none confirmed). Health care: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street; North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 2nd floor, 221 West Esplanade. Shopping: the District OCP's Maplewood Village Centre plans Old Dollarton Road, at the west end of Dollarton, as a key focus of pedestrian activity, lined with retail businesses with apartments and live/work units above; a grocery store by name on Dollarton Highway is UNVERIFIED.

Roads and transit: Dollarton Highway is the main road along the shore — west via Main Street to Phibbs Exchange and Highway 1 (including the Ironworkers Memorial Second Narrows Crossing), east to Deep Cove. TransLink route 211 (Phibbs Exchange / Burrard Station) runs via Dollarton Highway between Deep Cove and Phibbs Exchange, with some trips continuing to Burrard Station; route 212 runs via Dollarton Highway and Main Street to Phibbs Exchange; route 215 (Indian River) runs via Main Street, Dollarton Highway and Old Dollarton Road, then Riverside Drive and Mount Seymour Parkway. The R2 RapidBus connects at Phibbs Exchange and, since September 7, 2026, runs one-seat from Park Royal through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Dollarton

items.t: Hazard Development Permits (District frame — the live Dollarton checks): OCP Schedule B permit areas — natural-environment protection, streamside, wildfire, creek and slope — plus the shoreline record: Cates Park shoreline erosion worsening with sea level rise (port authority), District flood levels modelled to a 2100 horizon plus 0.6 m, and the 7.6 m Ocean Natural Boundary setback for waterfront principal buildings. Pull the GeoWeb flood construction level and get an insurance quote before subjects come off on a waterfront lot.

Foreshore layer (federal): Burrard Inlet waters and the intertidal area are port-authority-managed federal lands and waters — dock, seawall or foreshore work needs that check, not just a District permit.

Strata block (for completeness — no Dollarton bare-land strata stock is verified): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Dollarton ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

The reserve shoreline is part of the street's geography: the port authority's report places the Tsleil-Waututh Nation reserve lands (Burrard Inlet IR #3) along the shore backed by Dollarton Highway, between Maplewood Flats at the west end and Cates Park farther east — the land pattern a Dollarton Highway drive actually passes.

faq.a: The District of North Vancouver shore along Dollarton Highway on Burrard Inlet, between Maplewood Flats at the west end and Deep Cove to the east, taking in Whey-ah-Wichen (Cates Park) at 4141 Dollarton Highway and the Tsleil-Waututh Nation reserve shoreline.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Dollarton address?
faq.a: No public school inside Dollarton is confirmed. The schools beside the area are Cove Cliff Elementary (1818 Banbury Road) and Seycove Secondary (1204 Caledonia Avenue) in Deep Cove and Seymour Heights Elementary (2640 Carnation Street) to the north-west; catchments are address-based — check the exact address with SD44.

faq.q: What buses run on Dollarton Highway?
faq.a: Routes 211, 212 and 215 all run along Dollarton Highway to Phibbs Exchange, and some 211 trips continue over the Ironworkers Memorial Bridge to Burrard Station.

faq.q: What shoreline risks affect Dollarton waterfront homes?
faq.a: The port authority states the Cates Park shoreline is eroding and likely to worsen with sea level rise and climate change; District Schedule B creek, slope and wildfire permit areas can also apply, the District's flood levels are modelled to a 2100 horizon plus 0.6 m, and waterfront principal buildings need a 7.6 m setback from the Ocean Natural Boundary Line.

faq.q: Is Cates Landing in Dollarton or Roche Point?
faq.a: Both, depending on the source. Search Roche Point as well as Dollarton or the complex will not appear.

faq.q: How many homes are at Cates Landing, and how many are apartments?
faq.a: Developer-era sources state 95 residences total: 80 apartment residences and 15 waterfront townhouses, in a 4-storey complex completed in 2017 by Polygon. The townhouses are a separate form inside the same strata — confirm the specific unit's form and strata lot on title.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Cates Landing condo long-term, and can I have a pet?
faq.a: A current listing describes the complex as freehold strata and "pet & rental friendly," and the building directory states pets allowed with restrictions. Independently of any bylaw text, strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable for long-term rentals anywhere in BC since November 24, 2022. Pet terms are a Form B / filed-bylaw question.

faq.q: What is the shoreline risk beside the complex?
faq.a: The port authority states the Cates Park shoreline is eroding and likely to worsen with sea level rise and climate change, threatening park infrastructure and cultural sites; a District / Tsleil-Waututh shoreline adaptation project is under port-authority review. For the unit itself: check the strata's insurance and deductible position and the District GeoWeb flood construction level (modelled to 2100 plus 0.6 m) before subject removal.

faq.q: Is any part of the waterfront approval federal?
faq.a: Yes. Burrard Inlet's waters and intertidal area are port-authority-managed federal lands and waters, so foreshore, dock or seawall work needs that check in addition to District permits — relevant to the townhouse component's private yards opening onto the waterfront.

faq.q: Is there a townhouse complex in Dollarton I can buy into?
faq.a: No standalone townhouse complex is verified.

faq.q: Is Cates Landing in Dollarton or Roche Point?
faq.a: Search Roche Point as well as Dollarton or the complex will not appear.

faq.q: How many homes are at Cates Landing, and how many are townhouses?
faq.a: Developer-era sources state 95 residences total: 80 apartment residences and 15 waterfront townhouses, in a 4-storey complex completed in 2017 by Polygon. The townhouses are a separate form inside the same strata — confirm the specific unit's form and strata lot on title.
